newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka to limit national state of emergency.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka to limit national state of emergency.

text.p: The Sri Lankan government said on Thursday it would end a state of emergency in most parts of the country following a drop in violent incidents.
Parliament voted overwhelmingly in favour of a government proposal limiting the state of emergency to some districts in the island, currently in its 14th year of ethnic war.
The motion, introduced by Deputy Defence Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte earlier in the day, was adopted by the 225-member parliament with 117 votes in favour to 77 against. The rest abstained.
No serious incidents of violence had been reported in most parts of Sri Lanka over the last few months, Ratwatte said.

The government, however, will maintain the state of emergency in the capital Colombo and surrounding areas, northern and eastern provinces and some areas of northern Anuradhapura district, which are seen to be targets of rebel attacks.

The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels are fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in the island's north and east, and the country is usually on alert for possible rebel attacks on civilian or military targets.
Ratwatte told parliament that since a new military offensive launched in May, 19 officers and 359 soldiers have been killed. Seventy-six officers and 1,674 soldiers have been wounded.
Some 760 of the wounded soldiers have since returned to the battlefield, he added.
The offensive, codenamed "Operation Jayasikuru", or "Sure of Victory", is aimed at opening a strategic highway linking northern Jaffna peninsula with the rest of the island.
The offensive has been slowed recently by two fierce rebel counterattacks, in which scores of soldiers and rebels have die.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the conflict. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
